chapter: Race, pay and the color line
title: Black musicians and white women: the Cavaliers and Lee Allen
summary: The Cavaliers' painter disguise and the story of driving Lee Allen to a white woman's house.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you always have to be, did you watch yourself, like if you were approached by a white girl?

No. No, it just, you see, it's always how you carried yourself. You know, I think this is what it was. Now, I'm going to call it the Danny White Cavaliers. They had this thing, you know, in fact they had this. I remember one time, a policeman threw some bullets on the bandstand.

But the Cavaliers, down at the, because when it was out on the shelf, right by the canal. Yeah. But, see, I never had nothing like that to happen with me. But they were so much into the white girls. And all of them, you know how they used to do? And then, on Mondays, they would put on, I guess you heard this before. Yeah. They would put on a white, overall, like a painter. Get a white hat, get a bucket, paint bucket, paint brush. And they go to the white girl house, they're just born there to paint the house.
You never heard that? You never heard that? I never heard that one.
That's the way it was. He's just, that's the easy one.
Just a painter, just a painter, just a painter, just a painter.
I had an incident happen with me, with Lee Allen.
Lee Allen had this white lady that he was messing around with.

And this is way back in the game. And he told me, he said, bring him on Two Row Street, right off of St. Claude. I brought Lee Allen on Two Row Street and got him on the first block off of St. Claude. Lee Allen got off the car and he's standing behind the tree. And he said he had to wait until the light clicked, click, click. And he stood there and waited and the light clicked. And Lee Allen left. Now he left his horn in my car. He told me I'm supposed to wait for him, see. He go in the house, he get on, run, go in the house. And so I'm driving around the block, half hour, hour, two hours. Lee ain't never came out, so I left. And I brought Lee Allen home to my house. And he told me he just did be daylight out of the house. He might like to call him.
So what I'm saying is, this is the way it was. Yeah. But um.
So there was sort of a two-edged sword.
Yeah, yeah, right, two-edged sword. Now, uh. It could work. But it could be bad too, see, like it could have been bad for me. Suppose, what I'm doing, going around and around the block.
But that's the way it was, and the people that were into that.
